reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 describes a layered oxide on a different alloy (CoCrFeNiMn) at a much lower temperature (400°C) and notes Al has a minor effect, contradicting the premise of Al-driven selective oxidation. E2 discusses spallation resistance in unspecified alloys with Y addition, not the proposed alloy or mechanism. E3 reviews oxidation in other HEA compositions (e.g., Al0.6CrFeCoNi, AlxCoCrFeNi) and does not address the specific alloy, grain boundary oxidation, or reducing atmosphere behavior. No evidence supports the claimed mechanisms for this alloy.
premises: Selective oxidation of Cr, Ti, and Al at grain boundaries forms a layered, non-uniform oxide scale.
Oxide growth induces volume mismatch and growth stresses that cause spallation when exceeding interfacial cohesion.
Spallation exposes fresh metal, accelerating oxidation and intergranular cracking leading to catastrophic failure.
In reducing atmospheres, insufficient oxidation permits vacancy clustering and grain boundary weakening, causing embrittlement.
The proposed mechanisms are specific to the additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy with an FCC matrix.
